findings.why: webcontent.Path is used to build a filesystem path without validation or containment checks, so a stored path containing traversal sequences or an absolute path can cause reading arbitrary files outside webContentDir.
webcontent.Path is loaded from stored data without validation, and filepath.Join permits absolute paths or '..' traversal to escape webContentDir and read arbitrary files on the server.

webcontent.Path is a stored value used directly in filesystem path construction, so an absolute path or traversal segments can escape webContentDir and cause arbitrary file reads when serializing website content.

It interpolates the user-controlled namespace value directly into a regular expression after only replacing '*' with '.*', so regex metacharacters in the namespace can broaden matches and bypass intended AuthorizationPolicy principal restrictions.

It builds an authentication principal regex by inserting unescaped namespace and service-account strings into the pattern, allowing regex metacharacters in policy values to match unintended SPIFFE identities and bypass authorization constraints.

serviceAccountRegex interpolates the namespace and service-account strings directly into a regular expression without escaping regex metacharacters, so a crafted value can alter the match and cause principals outside the intended service account/namespace to be accepted.

It interpolates the user-controlled namespace value into a regex after only replacing '*' with '.*' and without regexp.QuoteMeta, so regex metacharacters in the namespace can broaden matching and bypass intended AuthorizationPolicy principal restrictions.

The code reads files using filepath.Join(webContentDir, webcontent.Path) without validating that webcontent.Path stays within webContentDir, so a crafted stored path such as '../../etc/passwd' can cause arbitrary file read when serializing website content.

The unvalidated volumeContext value for MountTargetIp is concatenated directly into a mount option string (mountOptions = append(mountOptions, MountTargetIp+"="+ipAddr)), allowing a caller who controls volume attributes to inject additional mount options via delimiter characters.

Untrusted policy input `value` is interpolated into a regular expression without escaping, allowing regex metacharacters in namespace or service account names to alter the match semantics and potentially broaden authorization beyond the intended identity.

The namespace policy value is transformed by only replacing `*` with `.*` and then embedded directly into a regex, so other regex metacharacters in untrusted input can change the pattern and match unintended principals.

findings.location: parseVolumeId() used by NodePublishVolume, subpath handling in source := fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s", fsid, subpath)
findings.why: The volumeHandle mountPath/subpath is accepted from the request and only normalized with path.Clean without enforcing an allowed base or rejecting '..', allowing a caller that can issue NodePublishVolume requests to mount arbitrary EFS paths outside the intended access-point or application directory.

checkType performs unchecked type assertions on untrusted JSON fields (m["signed"].(map[string]any)["_type"].(string)), so a malformed metadata file can trigger a panic and cause denial of service instead of returning an error.
these functions call os.ReadFile on attacker-controlled paths and deserialize/hash the entire file in memory without size limits, enabling memory-exhaustion denial of service with large files.

checkType performs unchecked type assertions on attacker-controlled JSON (`m["signed"].(map[string]any)["_type"].(string)`), so malformed metadata lacking `signed` or `_type` or using unexpected JSON types will panic and can crash a client that parses untrusted metadata.

Untrusted JSON passed via FromBytes/FromFile reaches checkType, where missing or non-object/non-string signed/_type fields trigger unchecked type-assertion panics, causing a denial of service instead of returning an error.
